AI security just entered a new era.

This week Anthropic disclosed that roughly 25,000 fraudulent accounts were allegedly used to probe Claude through tens of millions of interactions — systematically extracting the model's capabilities from the outside in.

This is not a traditional cyberattack. No database was breached. No credentials were stolen. Instead, adversaries conducted what amounts to behavioral reverse engineering at industrial scale — mapping how a frontier AI reasons, where its limits sit, and what it can truly do.

For business leaders, the implication is immediate. The AI models powering your products and operations are themselves an attack surface. Competitors and bad actors do not need your training data if they can reconstruct your model's behavior through millions of carefully designed queries.

The era of treating model access as a simple API key is ending. Expect behavioral anomaly detection, inference-layer security, and model IP protection to become standard requirements in every serious enterprise AI deployment.

Security strategy must evolve as fast as capability strategy.
